assets.subject: A compact, high three-quarter sculpted CARTOON 3D field-shelter teaching diorama on warm off-white, visually matching the accepted S1-01 miniature pilot, with believable cloth, shade fabric, field soil and plastic materials. It is a distinct worked-case SCENE, not a duplicate of the existing single heat-reading tableau: show a clearly artificial faceless FULL training mannequin, unmistakably a nonhuman rigid display prop with visible smooth joint construction, safely seated under a nearby shade canopy. A small quiet fan, two unused damp cooling cloths and a blank mock-call phone rest on a separate low table. Sparse moisture beads on the synthetic surface make sweating possible, without asserting severity or a diagnosis. Show an empty clear path to the shade; NO distant vehicle, oral drink, medication, real person, hands, detached limb, visible caregiver, printed diagram, arrows, numbers, letters, fake text, brands or logos. No first-aid action is happening; the narration/editable overlays carry the alertness, swallowing and escalation decisions. Keep generous clean margins and a compact sculpted educational form, never a photoreal hospital scene or toy character.

A compact sculpted CARTOON 3D field-training diorama on warm off-white in the approved S1-01 miniature visual language, with realistic grass, soil, barrier and fabric textures but visibly not photography. Side THREE-QUARTER view along a narrow crop path: a shallow partly grass-concealed hole is clearly exposed as a training hazard, with a continuous small boundary keeping an empty safe approach away from its edge. A clearly synthetic faceless full training mannequin with smooth display joints lies STILL on stable ground beside the hole in the found position, entire body supported, ankle untouched. Place a blank emergency-location card outside the boundary as an unused prop. No actual injury, twisted or detached body part, blood, helper, person, hands, pulling, lifting, straightening, forced walking, confirmed fracture icon, labels, numbers, arrows, symbols, brands or pseudo-writing. Leave margins for later localized overlays. The original source scenario's call-and-do-not-manipulate decisions are explained by speech, not baked into the pixels.

A compact sculpted CARTOON 3D safety-training route on warm off-white, same owner-accepted S1-01 miniature style with plausible brushed metal, ceramic and clean plastic texture. Medium LOW side view different from the existing chemical-reading route: in the near foreground an UNOPENED neutral plain training bottle stands upright on a clear table, well away from a full fixed dual-nozzle eyewash unit visibly connected to a wall pipe in the far but clear reachable station. The broad walkway between props is unobstructed. The eyewash is intact and unused, with no activated spray or person. Keep an empty clean space for editable four-language action overlays. No actual fertilizer release, eye, face, human, mannequin, hand, helper, small bottle as sole washing provision, chemical symbol, text, arrows, numbers, logos, pseudo-writing or real treatment. Never depict a fixed wash duration; the actual product SDS and medical guidance govern the spoken lesson.

A compact sculpted CARTOON 3D educational comparison in the accepted S1-01 warm off-white diorama style, with believable clean gauze, tape, folded blanket, plastic and metal textures. A THREE-QUARTER close view of two separate UNUSED response-prop stations, intentionally unlike the existing open-kit inventory video scene: left, a sealed clean gauze pack and tape beside a folded emergency blanket; centre, one entirely BLANK contact card and blank mock-call phone; right, a full fixed plumbed dual-nozzle eyewash unit clearly separated from a small closed starter eye-rinse bottle. The bottle must not look like sufficient sole provision. A modest training kit sits closed in the background to distinguish this reasoned-selection case from the earlier open-kit shot. Nothing touches a body and no care is performed. No person, hand, mannequin, wound, embedded object, tweezers in use, medicine, labels, printed lines, arrows, numbers, symbols, logos, branding or pseudo-writing. Leave clean margins for localized editable callouts.
